subject: math
title: Single Transformations: Slides, Flips and Turns on a Grid
seo_title: Grade 5 Math: Single Transformations Worksheets – Slides, Flips and Turns (Free, BC Curriculum, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on single transformations for the BC curriculum: slide (translate), flip (reflect) and turn (rotate) shapes on a grid, tell which transformation was used and read points in the first quadrant. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A slide moves, a flip makes a mirror image, a turn goes around a point. The shape never changes size.
key_sub: Count the jumps, not the square you start on. In a flip each point stays the same distance from the line. In a turn the centre does not move.
body_html:
Three ways to move a shape

A transformation moves a shape to a new place. In Grade 5 you do one move at a time: a slide (translation), a flip (reflection) or a turn (rotation). The shape keeps its size and its angles. Only its place, or the way it faces, changes.

MoveWhat happensWhich way it faces
Slide (translation)moves left or right and up or downthe same way
Flip (reflection)flips over a linemirror image
Turn (rotation)turns about a pointturned

Slides: count the jumps

In a slide every vertex moves the same number of units in the same direction. Count the jumps from one grid point to the next. Do not count the point you start on.

Example

A point slides 5 units right. How do you count?

Put your finger on the point. Say “one” on the first jump, not on the start. Stop when you say “five”.

Answer: 5 jumps right

Flips: the same distance from the line

A flip makes a mirror image over a line of reflection. Each vertex ends up the same distance from the line, on the other side.

Example

A vertex is 2 units left of a vertical line. Where is its image?

Count 2 jumps to the line. Then count 2 more jumps past it. The line itself is not a jump.

Answer: 2 units right of the line

Turns: quarter turns and half turns

A turn moves a shape around a point called the centre of rotation. The centre does not move. Say how far and which way: a quarter turn is 90°, a half turn is 180°. Clockwise is the way clock hands move; counterclockwise is the other way.

Turnright becomesup becomes
quarter turn clockwisedownright
quarter turn counterclockwiseupleft
half turn (either way)leftdown

Flip or turn?

A flip changes only one thing: left and right swap, or top and bottom swap. A half turn swaps both: the shape is upside down and back to front.

Coordinates in the first quadrant

A point on a grid is named by two numbers: (x, y). Start at the origin, (0, 0). Go across first (x), then up (y).

Example

Point (2, 6) slides 3 units right. Where does it land?

Right changes x: 2 + 3 = 5. y stays 6.

Answer: (5, 6)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the start square or point as “one”Say “one” on the first jump
Counting the line of reflection as a jumpGo the same distance on the other side
Calling a half turn a flipUpside down and back to front is a half turn
Sliding a shape when it should be flippedA flip faces the other way
Turning the wrong wayClockwise goes like clock hands: from 12 towards 3
Swapping x and yGo across first (x), then up (y)

faq.q: What are single transformations in BC Grade 5 math?
faq.a: In the BC Grade 5 curriculum (Geometry and measurement), students do one transformation at a time on a grid: a slide (translation), a flip (reflection) or a turn (rotation), and they describe how the shape moved.

faq.q: What is the difference between a slide, a flip and a turn?
faq.a: A slide moves a shape without changing the way it faces, a flip makes a mirror image over a line, and a turn moves it around a point. None of them changes the shape’s size or angles.

faq.q: How can you tell a flip from a half turn?
faq.a: A flip swaps only left and right, or only top and bottom. A half turn swaps both, so the shape ends up upside down and back to front.

faq.q: Why do students land one square short when they slide a shape?
faq.a: They often say “one” on the square or point where they start. Count “one” on the first jump instead, and the shape lands in the right place.

items.q: Which sentence is true about a slide (translation)?
c: The shape faces the same way
The shape turns about a point
The shape becomes a mirror image
items.e: A slide moves a shape left or right and up or down. It does not flip or turn, so the shape faces the same way and keeps its size.

items.q: A triangle slides 5 units left. Its top vertex moves 5 units left. How does its bottom-right vertex move?
items.e: In a slide every vertex moves the same distance in the same direction. So every vertex moves 5 units left.

items.q: A square with sides of 4 cm slides 3 units up on grid paper. How long are its sides now?
items.e: A slide only moves the square. It does not stretch it, so the sides are still 4 cm long.

items.q: Point P slides 4 units right. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From P, count 4 jumps right. Count the jumps, not the point you start on. P lands on point C. Point A: 1 unit short (the starting point was counted as 1). Point B: it went up, not across. Point D: it went the wrong way.

items.q: Point P slides 3 units down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From P, count 3 jumps down. Count the jumps, not the point you start on. P lands on point B. Point A: 1 unit short (the starting point was counted as 1). Point C: it went the wrong way. Point D: it went right, not down.

items.q: Point P slides 5 units right and 3 units up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From P, count 5 jumps right and 3 jumps up. Count the jumps, not the point you start on. P lands on point A. Point B: 1 unit short (the starting point was counted as 1). Point C: the two moves were mixed up. Point D: only the move right was made.

items.q: Point P slides 5 units left and 4 units up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From P, count 5 jumps left and 4 jumps up. Count the jumps, not the point you start on. P lands on point D. Point A: 1 unit short (the starting point was counted as 1). Point B: only the move left was made. Point C: 1 unit too far.

items.q: Point A slides to point B. Describe the slide.
items.e: A is at (2, 3) and B is at (6, 3). Across: 2 to 6 is 4 units right. The y-coordinate stays 3, so there is no move up or down. Count the jumps, not the point you start on.

items.q: Point A slides to point B. Describe the slide.
items.e: A is at (5, 7) and B is at (5, 2). The x-coordinate stays 5, so there is no move left or right. Up and down: 7 to 2 is 5 units down. Count the jumps, not the point you start on.

items.q: Point A slides to point B. Describe the slide.
items.e: A is at (1, 1) and B is at (6, 4). Across: 1 to 6 is 5 units right. Up and down: 1 to 4 is 3 units up. Count the jumps, not the point you start on.

items.q: Point A slides to point B. Describe the slide.
items.e: A is at (7, 6) and B is at (2, 2). Across: 7 to 2 is 5 units left. Up and down: 6 to 2 is 4 units down. Count the jumps, not the point you start on.

items.q: The green shape slides 5 units right. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: In a slide the shape faces the same way, and every vertex moves 5 units right. Only D shows that. Others: A: a flip (mirror image), not a slide; B: 1 unit short (the starting point was counted as 1); C: a turn (the shape is upside down), not a slide.

items.q: The green shape slides 4 units down. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: In a slide the shape faces the same way, and every vertex moves 4 units down. Only C shows that. Others: A: a turn (the shape is upside down), not a slide; B: a flip (mirror image), not a slide; D: 1 unit short (the starting point was counted as 1).

items.q: Shape A slides to shape B. Describe the slide.
items.e: Follow one vertex. The vertex of A at (1, 5) moves to (6, 1) in B. That is 5 units right and 4 units down. Every vertex moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A slides to shape B. Describe the slide.
items.e: Follow one vertex. The vertex of A at (6, 5) moves to (1, 1) in B. That is 5 units left and 4 units down. Every vertex moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A slides to shape B. Describe the slide.
items.e: Follow one vertex. The vertex of A at (6, 1) moves to (1, 5) in B. That is 5 units left and 4 units up. Every vertex moves the same way.

items.q: A point slides 3 units right, then 2 more units right. Describe this as one slide.
items.e: Both moves go right, so add them: 3 + 2 = 5. It is one slide of 5 units right.

items.q: A shape slides 6 units right. One vertex started 2 units from the left edge of the grid. How far from the left edge is it now?
items.e: Sliding right moves the vertex farther from the left edge: 2 + 6 = 8 units. (7 comes from counting the starting point as 1.)

items.q: Lucas slides a counter 5 units right. He says “one” on the starting point and stops when he says “five”. How far did the counter really move?
items.e: Saying “one” on the starting point does not move the counter. Only 4 of the counts are jumps, so it moved 4 units: 1 unit short. Count “one” on the first jump.

items.q: Sofia slides a shape 4 units down, but her image is 4 units above the shape. What mistake did she make?
c: She moved it the wrong way
items.e: Down makes the shape lower on the grid. The image is higher, so Sofia moved it up instead of down. The distance, 4 units, is right.

items.q: What does a flip (reflection) make?
c: a mirror image of the shape
a bigger copy of the shape
the same shape, facing the same way
a smaller copy of the shape
items.e: A flip turns the shape over a line, like a mirror. The image faces the other way, but its size does not change.

items.q: Point P is 3 units to the left of a vertical line of reflection. Where is its image?
c: 6 units to the right of the line
3 units to the right of the line
3 units to the left of the line
2 units to the right of the line
items.e: In a flip the image is the same distance from the line as the point, on the other side. (2 units comes from counting the line as the first jump.)

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line x = 4. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (2, 3) is 2 units to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 2 units to the right of it: 4 + 2 = 6. y stays 3. The image is (6, 3). That is point B. Point A: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point C: it was flipped up or down, not across the line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line x = 5. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (8, 6) is 3 units to the right of the line x = 5. The image is 3 units to the left of it: 5 − 3 = 2. y stays 6. The image is (2, 6). That is point A. Point B: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point C: it stops on the line of reflection. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line y = 3. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (2, 1) is 2 units below the line y = 3. The image is 2 units above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 2. The image is (2, 5). That is point D. Point A: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point B: x and y are swapped. Point C: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line.

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line y = 4. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (5, 6) is 2 units above the line y = 4. The image is 2 units below it: 4 − 2 = 2. x stays 5. The image is (5, 2). That is point C. Point A: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point B: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: The green shape is flipped (reflected) in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only D is a true mirror image. Others: A: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it faces the same way); B: the image is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump); C: the shape was turned (it is upside down and back to front), not flipped.

items.q: The green shape is flipped (reflected) in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only A is a true mirror image. Others: B: the image is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump); C: the shape was flipped the wrong way (left to right), not over the dashed line; D: the shape was turned (it is upside down and back to front), not flipped.

items.q: The green shape is flipped (reflected) in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only B is a true mirror image. Others: A: the image is 1 unit too far from the line; C: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it faces the same way); D: the shape was turned (it is upside down and back to front), not flipped.

items.q: Reflect the point (3, 4) in the vertical line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (3, 4) is 2 units to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 2 units to the right of it: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4. The image is (7, 4).

items.q: Reflect the point (6, 9) in the horizontal line y = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (6, 9) is 3 units above the line y = 6. The image is 3 units below it: 6 − 3 = 3. x stays 6. The image is (6, 3).

items.q: Reflect the point (8, 2) in the vertical line x = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (8, 2) is 2 units to the right of the line x = 6. The image is 2 units to the left of it: 6 − 2 = 4. y stays 2. The image is (4, 2).

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the vertical line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is on the line of reflection x = 5, so it does not move: (5, 3). A point on the line of reflection is its own image.

items.q: The point (4, 2) is reflected in the horizontal line y = 5. How many units apart are the point and its image?
items.e: (4, 2) is 3 units below y = 5, so the image (4, 8) is 3 units above it. From the point to the image is 3 + 3 = 6 units. (3 is only the distance to the line.)

items.q: The points (2, 6) and (8, 6) are reflections of each other. Where is the line of reflection?
items.e: The line is halfway between the points. From 2 to 8 is 6 units, and half of 6 is 3. 2 + 3 = 5, so the line is x = 5. (y = 6 goes through both points; it is not between them.)

items.q: Nadia wants to flip shape A in the dashed line. Is shape B correct?
c: No, it is 1 unit too close to the line
No, it was turned, not flipped
No, it was slid, not flipped
items.e: Check each vertex. The vertex (1, 1) is 3 units below the line y = 4. The image is 3 units above it: 4 + 3 = 7. x stays 1. The image is (1, 7). Every vertex works the same way, so B is a correct mirror image.

items.q: Mei wants to flip shape A in the dashed line. Is shape B correct?
c: No, it is 1 unit too close to the line
No, it was turned, not flipped
No, it was slid, not flipped
items.e: (1, 1) is 4 units from the line x = 5, so its image should be at (9, 1). B has that vertex at (8, 1): 1 unit too close. The line was counted as the first jump.

items.q: Leah wants to flip shape A in the dashed line. Is shape B correct?
c: No, it is 1 unit too close to the line
No, it was turned, not flipped
No, it was slid, not flipped
items.e: In A the right angle is at the bottom left. A flip over y = 4 would put it at the top left, at (2, 7). In B the right angle is at the top right: B is A turned upside down and back to front. That is a turn, not a flip.

items.q: Ethan flips a right triangle in a vertical line. His image points the same way as the triangle. What mistake did he make?
c: He slid it instead of flipping it
items.e: A flip makes a mirror image, so it faces the other way. If the image points the same way, the shape was slid (translated).

items.q: A point is 4 units from a line of reflection. Liam counts “one” on the line and stops at “four”. How far from the line is his image?
items.e: Counting “one” on the line uses up a count without a jump. Only 3 jumps were made, so the image is 3 units from the line. It should be 4 units away, the same as the point.

items.q: How many degrees is a quarter turn?
items.e: A full turn is 360°. A quarter turn is one of 4 equal parts: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°. A half turn is 180°.

items.q: Which way do the hands of a clock turn?
items.e: Clock hands go from 12 to 3 to 6 to 9: that is clockwise. The other way is counterclockwise.

items.q: The minute hand of a clock moves from 12 to 3. What turn is that?
items.e: From 12 to 3 is one quarter of the way around the clock, and clock hands move clockwise.

items.q: A triangle is turned about its vertex A. Which point stays in the same place?
items.e: The centre of rotation (the turn centre) does not move. Here it is vertex A; every other point turns around it.

items.q: A shape makes two quarter turns clockwise about the same point. What is that the same as?
items.e: Each quarter turn is 90°. 90° + 90° = 180°, which is a half turn.

items.q: A shape is turned 180° clockwise about a point. A copy of it is turned 180° counterclockwise about the same point. Where do they land?
c: one lands twice as far away
one is a mirror image of the other
items.e: A half turn is a half turn, whichever way you go. 180° clockwise and 180° counterclockwise end in the same place.

items.q: Turn the point B (6, 4) 90° clockwise about the point A (3, 4). Where does B land?
items.e: From A (3, 4), B (6, 4) is 3 right. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (3, 4), the image is 3 down: (3, 1).

items.q: Turn the point Q (8, 5) 90° counterclockwise about the point P (5, 5). Where does Q land?
items.e: From P (5, 5), Q (8, 5) is 3 right. In a 90° counterclockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So from (5, 5), the image is 3 up: (5, 8).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices K (3, 3), L (5, 3), M (5, 6) and N (3, 6). It is turned 90° clockwise about vertex K. Where does vertex M land?
items.e: From vertex K (3, 3), vertex M (5, 6) is 2 right and 3 up. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (3, 3), the image is 3 right and 2 down: (6, 1).

items.q: A triangle has vertices A (4, 4), B (1, 5) and C (4, 7). It is turned 180° about vertex A. Where does vertex B land?
items.e: From vertex A (4, 4), vertex B (1, 5) is 3 left and 1 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (4, 4), the image is 3 right and 1 down: (7, 3).

items.q: The green shape is turned 90° clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go down in a quarter turn (90°) clockwise. Only B shows that. Others: A: a half turn (180°); C: a quarter turn counterclockwise; D: a flip (mirror image), not a turn.

items.q: The green shape is turned 90° counterclockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go up in a quarter turn (90°) counterclockwise. Only A shows that. Others: B: a flip (mirror image), not a turn; C: a half turn (180°); D: a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: The green shape is turned 180° about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go left in a half turn (180°). Only D shows that. Others: A: a flip (mirror image), not a turn; B: a quarter turn counterclockwise; C: a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: The green shape is turned 90° clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going up turns to go right in a quarter turn (90°) clockwise. Only C shows that. Others: A: a half turn (180°); B: a flip (mirror image), not a turn; D: a quarter turn counterclockwise.

items.q: Point P is turned 90° clockwise about point R. Which point is the image?
items.e: From R (4, 3), P (7, 5) is 3 right and 2 up. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (4, 3), the image is 2 right and 3 down: (6, 0). That is point A. Point B: turned the wrong way (90° counterclockwise). Point C: a 180° turn, not 90°. Point D: the numbers were swapped, but the directions were not turned.

items.q: Point P is turned 180° about point R. Which point is the image?
items.e: From R (5, 4), P (3, 7) is 2 left and 3 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (5, 4), the image is 2 right and 3 down: (7, 1). That is point D. Point A: a 90° turn clockwise, not 180°. Point B: a 90° turn counterclockwise, not 180°. Point C: the numbers were swapped, but the directions were not turned.

items.q: A shape is turned about its vertex (4, 4). Another vertex moves from (6, 4) to (4, 2). Describe the turn.
items.e: (6, 4) is 2 right from the centre. (4, 2) is 2 down from the centre. Right turned into down: that is a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: A shape is turned about its vertex (3, 3). Another vertex moves from (5, 4) to (1, 2). Describe the turn.
items.e: (5, 4) is 2 right and 1 up from the centre. (1, 2) is 2 left and 1 down from the centre. Right turned into left and up turned into down: that is a half turn, 180°.

items.q: Ryan turns the point (7, 3) 90° clockwise about (4, 3) and gets (4, 6). What mistake did he make?
items.e: (4, 6) is a quarter turn counterclockwise. From the centre (4, 3), the point (7, 3) is 3 right. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (4, 3), the image is 3 down: (4, 0).

items.q: Hana turns an L-shape a half turn. Her image has the foot of the L still at the bottom, but pointing the other way. What mistake did she make?
c: She flipped it instead of turning it
She turned it a quarter turn
items.e: After a half turn the L is upside down, so the foot ends up at the top. A foot still at the bottom but pointing the other way is a mirror image: a flip.

sets.title: Which transformation? Slide, flip or turn

items.q: Which transformation is most like SkyTrain moving along a straight piece of track?
items.e: The train moves in a straight line and does not turn or flip, so it is a slide.

items.q: Which transformation is most like the mountains and their upside-down picture in a calm lake?
items.e: The picture in the water is a mirror image, upside down over the shoreline. That is a flip.

items.q: Which transformation is most like a door swinging open on its hinges?
items.e: The door turns about the hinges. The hinges stay still, like a turn centre. That is a turn.

items.q: Which transformation is most like pushing a box straight across the gym floor?
items.e: The box moves across without turning or flipping, so it is a slide.

items.q: Which transformation is most like the hands of a clock moving from 12 to 6?
items.e: The hands turn about the centre of the clock. That is a half turn.

items.q: Which transformation is most like your hand and its image in a mirror?
items.e: A mirror image faces the other way: a right hand looks like a left hand. That is a flip.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B faces the same way as A and is the same size. Every vertex moved 5 units right and 3 units up, for example (1, 1) → (6, 4). That is a slide.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B is a mirror image of A: the foot of the L points the other way, but it is still at the bottom. It is a flip in the line x = 5.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the long arm of the L lies flat along the bottom. In B it stands straight up. A slide or a flip cannot make a flat arm stand up, but a turn can: B is A turned a quarter turn (90°) clockwise.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B looks exactly like A and faces the same way. Every vertex moved 5 units right and 4 units down. That is a slide.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the right angle is at the bottom left; in B it is at the top left. B is A flipped over the line y = 4: each vertex is the same distance from the line on the other side. That is a flip.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B is A upside down and back to front: a half turn (180°) about the vertex (5, 2). A flip would change only one of these.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: Follow the top edge of A, from (1, 5) to (5, 5): it goes across. In B the same edge goes up and down, from (6, 1) to (6, 5). A slide or a flip cannot do that, but a turn can: B is A turned a quarter turn (90°) counterclockwise.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the long side is at the bottom; in B it is at the top, and the square corners are still on the left. That is a mirror image over the line y = 4: a flip. A half turn would also move the square corners to the right.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the right angle is at the bottom left. In B it is at the top right: upside down and back to front. That is a half turn. A flip would change only one of these.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: A is 4 units by 2 units. B is only 2 units by 1 unit, so B is smaller. A slide, a flip or a turn never changes the size.

items.q: In which transformation does one point always stay still?
items.e: In a turn the centre of rotation does not move. In a slide every point moves. In a flip only points on the line stay still, and a shape does not have to touch the line.

items.q: After which transformation does the shape always face the same way?
items.e: A slide only moves the shape. A flip makes a mirror image, and a turn changes the way it points.

items.q: Owen sees an L-shape and its image. The image is upside down and back to front. He says it is a flip. Is he right?
c: No. It is a half turn
items.e: A flip changes only one thing: left to right, or up to down. Upside down and back to front together is a half turn (180°).

items.q: Shape B is a mirror image of shape A. How could you check?
c: Fold the paper along a line and see if they match
items.e: A flip line works like a fold. If A lands exactly on B when you fold the paper, B is a flip of A.

sets.title: Coordinates in the first quadrant: word problems

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 3, then go up 5. Point A is at (3, 5). The x-coordinate (across) is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 6, then go up 2. Point B is at (6, 2). The x-coordinate (across) is written first. (2, 6) is point C: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point G?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), do not move across, then go up 4. Point G is at (0, 4). The x-coordinate (across) is written first. A point on the y-axis has x-coordinate 0.

items.q: Which point is at (4, 2)?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 4, then go up 2: that is point C. Point A is at (2, 4): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (1, 6)?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 1, then go up 6: that is point B. Point A is at (6, 1): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: To plot the point (6, 3), what do you do first from the origin?
items.e: The first number, 6, is the x-coordinate. It tells you how far to go across, so go right 6. Then go up 3.

items.q: Noah plots the point (2, 5). He starts at the origin, goes up 2, then right 5. What mistake did he make?
items.e: In (2, 5), x = 2 comes first: go right 2, then up 5. Noah went up 2 and right 5, so he plotted (5, 2).

items.q: A point is on the x-axis, 8 units to the right of the origin. What are its coordinates?
items.e: 8 units right gives x = 8. The point is on the x-axis, so it does not go up: y = 0. The point is (8, 0).

items.q: In a coding lesson, Zara’s robot starts at (1, 2). The code says: move 4 right, then move 3 up. Where does the robot stop?
items.e: Right 4 changes x: 1 + 4 = 5. Up 3 changes y: 2 + 3 = 5. The new point is (5, 5).

items.q: Kai’s robot is at (2, 7). He wants it to stop at (6, 3). Which code works?
items.e: The start is at (2, 7) and the end is at (6, 3). Across: 2 to 6 is 4 units right. Up and down: 7 to 3 is 4 units down. Count the jumps, not the point you start on.

items.q: In a board game, each turn moves a counter 2 units right. Mateo’s counter starts at (1, 4). Where is it after 3 turns?
items.e: 3 turns is 3 × 2 = 6 units right. x: 1 + 6 = 7. y stays 4. The counter is at (7, 4).

items.q: On a map of a campground near Kamloops, the fire pit is at (3, 5) and the canoe dock is at (8, 1). Describe the slide from the fire pit to the dock.
items.e: The fire pit is at (3, 5) and the dock is at (8, 1). Across: 3 to 8 is 5 units right. Up and down: 5 to 1 is 4 units down. Count the jumps, not the point you start on.

items.q: On a lacrosse play diagram, Emma runs from (2, 3), 6 units right and 4 units up. Where does she stop?
items.e: Right 6 changes x: 2 + 6 = 8. Up 4 changes y: 3 + 4 = 7. The new point is (8, 7).

items.q: On a map of Stanley Park, the totem poles are at (4, 1) and the lighthouse is at (4, 7). How many units apart are they?
items.e: The x-coordinates are the same, so the lighthouse is straight up from the totem poles. From 1 up to 7 is 7 − 1 = 6 units. (7 comes from counting the starting point as 1.)

items.q: Ava makes a paper snowflake for the class window. The design is symmetrical in the line x = 5. One tip is at (2, 6). Where is the matching tip?
items.e: The tip (2, 6) is 3 units to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 3 units to the right of it: 5 + 3 = 8. y stays 6. The image is (8, 6).

items.q: A class banner is symmetrical in the horizontal line y = 5. One corner is at (3, 2). Where is the matching corner?
items.e: The corner (3, 2) is 3 units below the line y = 5. The image is 3 units above it: 5 + 3 = 8. x stays 3. The image is (3, 8).

items.q: A school garden has a path along the line x = 5. A garden bed with vertices at (1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 4), (1, 4) is flipped over the path to make a matching bed. Which list shows the vertices of the new bed?
items.e: Each vertex goes the same distance on the other side of x = 5: (1, 2) is 4 units left, so its image is 4 units right, at (9, 2). (3, 2) is 2 units left, so its image is (7, 2).

items.q: Simran draws a pinwheel for a Terry Fox Run poster. One blade tip is at (7, 6). The next blade is the first one turned 90° counterclockwise about the centre (5, 5). Where is the next tip?
items.e: From the centre (5, 5), the tip (7, 6) is 2 right and 1 up. In a 90° counterclockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So from (5, 5), the image is 1 left and 2 up: (4, 7).

items.q: Jasleen makes a quilt pattern. A triangle has a vertex at (8, 7). She turns the triangle 180° about its vertex (6, 6). Where does the vertex at (8, 7) go?
items.e: From the centre (6, 6), the vertex (8, 7) is 2 right and 1 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (6, 6), the image is 2 left and 1 down: (4, 5).

items.q: A rug on a floor plan covers 6 squares. It is turned 90° about one corner. Which sentence is true?
items.e: A turn moves the rug but does not stretch it. The side lengths, angles and area stay the same, so it still covers 6 squares.
